fact_checks.rationale: FDA labeling, EMA EPAR, and PubMed RCT records identify the active substance/drug as cenobamate.
Xcopri is the FDA-approved US product name; Ontozry is the EMA/eMC product name for cenobamate. No evidence suggests either should be a separate generic-drug row.
No alternate INN/common generic name was identified. YKP3089 is a development code and is appropriately captured as a PubMed search alias rather than an alternate generic name.
YKP3089 is used in cenobamate trial titles and ClinicalTrials.gov records.
FDA approved Xcopri (cenobamate) tablets for partial-onset seizures in adult patients, and current FDA labeling is available.

The FDA NDA approval letter is electronically signed 11/21/2019. Note: current label highlights list Initial U.S. Approval as 2020, apparently reflecting controlled-substance scheduling/effective marketing timing, but the FDA approval action was in 2019.
FDA labeling uses partial-onset seizures, which maps to focal-onset terminology; EMA/eMC explicitly use focal-onset seizures.
FDA label lists oral tablets in 12.5, 25, 50, 100, 150, and 200 mg strengths; eMC lists Ontozry tablets/film-coated tablets.

fact_checks.current_value: Adults: titrate to 200 mg once daily; may increase to 400 mg/day
fact_checks.proposed_value: Adults: titrate to 200 mg once daily; may increase to 400 mg/day
fact_checks.rationale: FDA and eMC labeling support once-daily titration to a 200 mg/day target/maintenance dose, with increases up to 400 mg/day based on response and tolerability.
FDA and eMC labeling list 400 mg/day as the maximum daily dose in adults without hepatic dose limitation.

fact_checks.current_value: 100 mg/day showed efficacy in focal-onset RCTs; 200 mg/day recommended maintenance
fact_checks.proposed_value: 100 mg/day showed efficacy in focal-onset RCTs; 200 mg/day recommended maintenance
fact_checks.rationale: FDA Study 2 reports statistically significant seizure-frequency reduction for 100 mg/day versus placebo; FDA/eMC dosing recommends 200 mg/day as the target/maintenance dose.
FDA label states apparent terminal half-life is 50-60 hours over 100-400 mg/day.
FDA label states cenobamate is extensively metabolized and describes glucuronidation/oxidation pathways; hepatic impairment substantially increases exposure.

fact_checks.current_value: Inhibits CYP2C19; induces CYP3A4, CYP2B6, and UGT pathways
fact_checks.proposed_value: Inhibits CYP2C19; induces CYP3A4 and CYP2B6
fact_checks.rationale: FDA clinical interaction data support increased CYP2C19 substrate exposure and decreased CYP3A/CYP2B6 substrate exposure. Current FDA label also lists in vitro CYP2B6/CYP2C8/CYP3A4 induction and CYP2B6/CYP2C19/CYP3A inhibition, but I did not find FDA-label support for UGT induction.
The row's own enzyme text and FDA label both indicate clinically relevant induction and inhibition effects, so a filter containing only Inhibitor is incomplete.

fact_checks.current_value: Precise therapeutic mechanism is unknown; cenobamate reduces repetitive neuronal firing by inhibiting voltage-gated sodium currents and positively modulates GABA-A ion channels.
fact_checks.proposed_value: Precise therapeutic mechanism is unknown; cenobamate reduces repetitive neuronal firing by inhibiting voltage-gated sodium currents and positively modulates GABA-A ion channels.
fact_checks.rationale: FDA label directly supports this mechanism wording.
This is a curator confidence classification, not a directly source-verifiable drug fact. It is consistent with the FDA label statement that the precise therapeutic mechanism is unknown.
The mechanism is supported by FDA labeling; removing DailyMed from the source text makes the row align with the trusted-domain source policy.
The cited mechanism source tier is correct.

outcome_checks.current_value: 28.2-39 % (drug minus placebo RR50 differential at maximum effective dose/regimen: Chung2020 cenobamate 200 mg/day 28.2%; Krauss2019 cenobamate 400 mg/day 39%)
outcome_checks.proposed_value: 28.2-53.4 % (drug minus placebo RR50 differential at maximum effective dose/regimen: Lee2025 cenobamate 400 mg/day 53.4%; Chung2020 cenobamate 200 mg/day 28.2%; Krauss2019 cenobamate 400 mg/day 39%)
outcome_checks.rationale: Chung2020 and Krauss2019 differentials are correct. Lee2025/NCT04557085 reports an overall maintenance-phase >=50% responder rate for 400 mg/day of 81.6% versus 28.2% placebo, a 53.4 percentage-point differential, so the current maximum RR50 differential is too low if Lee2025 outcomes are included.
Plot values should include Lee2025 RR50 differential if the row includes Lee2025 as outcome evidence.

outcome_checks.current_value: 31-74.1 % (drug minus placebo MPC differential at maximum effective dose/regimen: Lee2025 cenobamate 400 mg/day 74.1%; Chung2020 cenobamate 200 mg/day 34.1%; Krauss2019 cenobamate 400 mg/day 31%)
outcome_checks.proposed_value: 31-74.1 % (drug minus placebo MPC differential at maximum effective dose/regimen: Lee2025 cenobamate 400 mg/day 74.1%; Chung2020 cenobamate 200 mg/day 34.1%; Krauss2019 cenobamate 400 mg/day 31%)
outcome_checks.rationale: Lee2025 reports -100.0% at 400 mg/day versus -25.9% placebo, differential 74.1. Chung2020 reports 55.6% versus 21.5%, differential 34.1. Krauss2019/FDA Study 2 reports about 55.3% versus 24.3%, differential 31.0.
The plotted MPC differential values match the cited RCT/outcome evidence.
